method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Puzzle”.
Name a type of physical robot.
questions.scope: Recognized scientific names and established public synonyms for the whole subject count. Different spellings of one identity score once. Unrelated everyday meanings and invented initials do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an ice-cream or frozen-dessert brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical ice-cream, gelato, frozen-custard, frozen-yogurt, sorbet, ice-pop and branded ice/slush treats count. Documented specialty chains, actual licensed product-line brands and store labels count. Different flavors, package sizes and unbranded desserts are not brands; neither pet food nor a company with no proven frozen-dessert product qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a hand tool or utensil used to prepare or serve food.
questions.scope: Kitchen hand tools, utensils, serving implements and nonpowered cookware count. Small measuring tools used in food preparation also count. Large powered appliances and foods do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a fairy tale or traditional folk tale.
questions.scope: Recognized named traditional folk tales and published literary fairy tales count, including documented fairy-tale novels. Actual translated/alternate titles of a tale share an answer. Whole anthologies, authors and arbitrary modern fantasy novels do not automatically qualify. Different tales are not merged merely because they have a shared ATU plot number or point to a shared character/collection article.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with rock music.
Name a kind of primate. Named groups and species, living or extinct, count; a common or scientific name is accepted.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a quarterback who started and won a Super Bowl.
questions.scope: The quarterback must have started a winning Super Bowl, through Super Bowl LX in February 2026. Winning a ring as a backup alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a video game console or dedicated gaming handheld.
questions.scope: Named released game consoles, dedicated handheld game systems and purpose-built gaming handheld PCs count. Named revisions, early electronic/VHS-based gaming systems and game-library add-on platforms count; regional renames of the same platform share an answer. N-Gage is a documented gaming-handheld hybrid. General-purpose phones/computers, media-streaming boxes with optional games, unreleased prototypes and input-only controllers do not count. A self-contained plug-and-play game unit counts even if its shell resembles a controller.

questions.prompt: Name a government-issued currency, monetary unit or named historical coin.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a branch or field of mathematics.
questions.scope: Recognized mathematical branches, subfields and established mathematical research disciplines count. Both pure and applied mathematics count. Individual formulas, symbols, isolated theorems and unrelated school subjects do not by themselves name a branch.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of flatbread.
questions.scope: Recognized flatbread types, named regional breads and flatbread dishes count, including leavened and unleavened types. Ordinary sandwich loaves, toppings and ingredients alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a romance movie.
Name a musical instrument with a keyboard.
questions.scope: Recognized keyboard-instrument types and documented named keyboard instruments or models count. Keys and buttons form the musical playing interface; having ordinary valves or attaching an external controller does not automatically qualify another instrument.

questions.prompt: Name a status effect in vanilla Minecraft.
questions.scope: Named status effects in unmodded Java or Bedrock Minecraft count, including command-only and edition-specific effects. Potion names map to the actual underlying effect.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a hotel chain or hotel brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical hotel, motel, hostel and serviced-apartment brands/chains, branded hotel collections and primarily hotel-operating groups count. Single independent properties, booking/rental marketplaces, private-equity investors and unrelated parent companies do not. Genuine short names and brand renames share an answer.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that is active at night.
questions.scope: Normally nocturnal or regularly night-active animals count; occasional unusual behavior does not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of clock, watch or timekeeping device.
questions.scope: Physical timekeeping devices and recognized clock/watch types count, including historic sundials, hourglasses and water clocks. Calendar systems, units of time and software applications alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a sauce, condiment, or relish served with food. Named traditional condiments count.
Name a song by Foo Fighters.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Foo Fighters count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a location that has appeared on a Fortnite Battle Royale map.
questions.scope: Named locations from any past or present Battle Royale season count.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the New York Knicks.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not.

questions.prompt: Name a car, motorcycle, truck or bus manufacturer or brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical manufacturers and established marques of cars, motorcycles (including racing motorcycles), trucks and buses count, including documented vehicle assembly and coachbuilding firms. A vehicle model alone, a transport operator, an aircraft/rail-only maker, a pure component supplier, a toy or a fictional brand does not count. Actual brand/company names and true renames share an answer.

questions.prompt: Name a chemical element used in everyday products.
questions.scope: There must be a documented consumer, industrial or medical use; exact product names are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a movie that is a sequel to another movie.
questions.scope: Direct sequels count, even if there is no number in the title.

questions.prompt: Name a type of puzzle or brain teaser.
questions.scope: Established puzzle forms and named puzzle families count: word, logic, number, visual, mathematical and mechanical puzzles, including actual named physical twisty-puzzle forms. A normal competitive game or a puzzle publisher, isolated article title, or generic software game title is not automatically a puzzle form.

questions.prompt: Name a bird that cannot normally fly, including extinct flightless birds.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Juice WRLD.
questions.scope: Released song titles with Juice WRLD as a lead or vocal guest count, including released mixtape songs and actual group performances. Production-only credits, unofficial leaks and instrumental-only versions do not count. Clean/explicit, live and remix variants share an answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a culinary nut or a seed people eat.
questions.scope: Culinary nuts and food seeds count, including grains, pulses, spice seeds and nuts that are not botanical nuts. Traditional foods that require preparation count. A named food seed or nut group counts; a botanical class, tree alone, finished sauce or book title does not.

questions.prompt: Name an athlete featured on a video game's cover or in its title.
questions.scope: An officially released sports game's cover athlete or title namesake qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a human blood vessel, blood-vessel type or named blood-vessel network.
questions.scope: Named human blood vessels, vessel types and recognized arterial/venous networks count, including real fetal vessels. Common vessel groups and proper anatomical names count. Heart chambers, lymph-only vessels, vessel-wall tissue, ligaments and ordinary blood cells do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an amusement park or theme-park resort.
questions.scope: Real parks and resort complexes count worldwide; familiar resort names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
questions.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

questions.prompt: Name a princess from fiction.
questions.scope: Characters who are, were, or are explicitly known as princesses count, along with the official Disney Princess lineup. A character does not qualify simply by being female, wearing a crown or appearing in a Disney movie.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a musical genre or subgenre.
Name a kind of arachnid.
questions.scope: Named arachnid groups, species and recognized common kinds count. Spiders, scorpions, ticks, mites, harvestmen and other arachnid orders are included. Insects, crustaceans and myriapods are outside this question.

questions.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a hormone or neurotransmitter made by the human body.
questions.scope: Documented natural human hormones/neurotransmitters and named groups count. Natural dual-role messengers count. Synthetic drug-only analogues and organs do not. Actual published abbreviations count; do not generate initials.

questions.prompt: Name a weapon or grenade in Counter-Strike 2. Knife types count.
questions.scope: Base weapons, explosives and knife models count; cosmetic finishes, gloves and healing items do not.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name an item or established style of clothing.
Name a type of building or place used for worship.
questions.scope: Types of religious worship building or built shrine count across religions. Individual named landmarks and a minister or deity alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a track on J. Cole’s Born Sinner.
questions.scope: The complete standard album and the five deluxe bonus tracks (also called Truly Yours 3) count, including named skits and interludes. Other albums and the separate Truly Yours and Truly Yours 2 EPs do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a chocolate bar or named chocolate-bar product.
questions.scope: Established named foods, products or varieties matching the whole subject count. Actual public synonyms share one identity. Invented ingredient combinations and generic descriptions do not create new answers.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has been on the Buffalo Bills franchise roster.
questions.scope: Past or present roster membership for this franchise through the retained 2026 snapshot counts, including its earlier names/locations and NFL, AFL or AAFC membership where applicable. Offseason and practice squads count. An unrelated former team sharing the same city or code does not. The current franchise rules and captured seasons are retained for source review.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of hummingbird.
questions.scope: Established named groups and species in the Trochilidae bird family count, including recently extinct species. Common and scientific names are accepted. Real synonyms share an identity; unrelated birds and objects named after birds do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a move from a Pokémon video game.
questions.scope: Named moves from released Pokémon games count, including Z-Moves, Max Moves and Colosseum/XD Shadow moves. Physical/special implementations of the same named move share one answer. Generic actions and moves from fan games do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a spy or secret agent from fiction.
questions.scope: Named fictional intelligence agents, spies, spymasters and documented clandestine/covert operatives from any medium count, including covert support agents and private fictional agencies. A secret identity, ordinary detective/police work, a group/show title, performer or an unnamed generic agent is not automatically a spy. Actual aliases share identity; different characters, clones and officeholders are not merged merely because they share a codename.

questions.prompt: Name a unit used to measure a physical quantity or digital information.
questions.scope: Established metric, customary, historical and scientific measurement units count, including named prefixed units. Currency units and arbitrary made-up units do not. Official unit symbols are accepted only when they name that actual unit.

questions.prompt: Name a river, lake, sea, ocean, gulf, bay or strait.
Name a dish made mainly from potatoes.
questions.scope: Named dishes count when potato is a main ingredient rather than a garnish.

questions.prompt: Name someone who has played in the WNBA.
Name something students bring to school.
questions.scope: Physical items brought for an ordinary school day count; people and pets do not.

questions.prompt: Name a musician known professionally by one name.
questions.scope: An established one-word stage name counts even when their legal name has several words.

questions.prompt: Name a block an Enderman can pick up in Minecraft.
questions.scope: The actual block-pickup rule counts, including flowers. Endermen may pick up only certain blocks even if the player can carry other blocks. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a comedy movie.
Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name a carnivorous plant.
questions.scope: Documented carnivorous plants and recognized named groups count. A whole mixed genus must not bring in non-carnivorous species. Fictional man-eating plants do not count. Cultivar epithets need their plant/genus qualification. Registered and independently documented cultivated forms count; a nomenclatural status alone does not decide real horticultural use.

questions.prompt: Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a named pasta or noodle dish.
questions.scope: Named dishes and established menu preparations count, including familiar meal names such as spaghetti, udon and soba, filled pastas and gnocchi. A bare unfilled pasta-shape name without a dish or established menu preparation does not count. Plain tteokbokki is a rice-cake dish; rabokki includes noodles.

questions.prompt: Name a holiday, traditional festival or recognized observance.
questions.scope: Real named religious/civic holidays, traditional festivals and established calendar observances count, including historical or regional observances and named periods such as Advent or Ramadan. Modern stand-alone concert/film festivals and conferences are a different subject. A calendar date, month, weekday, person, deity, place, ritual or campaign theme is not automatically an observance. Shared dates and related ancestry do not merge distinct observances; substitute dates do not create new ones.

questions.prompt: Name an online social or community platform.
questions.scope: Real current or historical general-audience social networks, social media and named online community platforms count, including group communication, public discussion networks and social virtual worlds. Ordinary email, devices, generic internet terms, individual profiles/groups, learning-management software and services dedicated to dating or adult content do not. Actual public names such as X, VK, QQ and Hi5 count; generated initials do not.

questions.prompt: Name a song by J. Cole.
questions.scope: Released song titles credited to J. Cole as a lead or vocal guest count, including mixtapes, released freestyles, collaborations and bonus tracks. Album names, production-only credits, unverified leaks and instrumental-only releases do not count. Clean/explicit, live and remix spellings of one title score once.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Toy Story franchise.
questions.scope: Named or distinctly identified characters from Toy Story films, shorts, series and the Lightyear spin-off count. Established collective character identities such as the Aliens count. Voice actors, film titles and descriptive organizational headings do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that makes a regular seasonal migration.
questions.scope: Named species and animal groups with documented recurring seasonal, breeding or feeding migrations count, including migrating populations of a species. One-off escapes or an individual simply wandering do not.

questions.prompt: Name a computer or device operating system.
questions.scope: Named actual current/historical operating systems, public OS families and documented Linux distributions count. Versions may expand answers but never prompts. Vendor, hardware, shell, desktop environment, app and proposed-only marketing labels are not automatically operating systems.

questions.prompt: Name a food that is commonly pickled.
questions.scope: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, meats and seafood with established pickled preparations count. Vinegar and brine are ingredients, not foods being pickled.

questions.prompt: Name a free-to-play PC or console game.
questions.scope: Games with an officially free base version count; a temporary free weekend does not.

questions.prompt: Name a passenger train or named passenger-rail service.
questions.scope: Real named passenger trains, branded scheduled services and named tourist trains count, including historical services. Fictional trains and vehicle manufacturers do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of ball used in a sport, game or athletic training.
questions.scope: Named balls used in sports, games or athletic training count, including particular game-ball designs. Pucks, shuttlecocks and punching bags are not balls.

questions.prompt: Name a dance style, traditional dance, or named social dance.
Name a type of flower.
questions.scope: Recognized common flower types and flowering plants grown for their blooms count, including named horticultural groups and documented varieties. Materials merely named after flowers, artificial flower products and unrelated decorative objects do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a material or substance used to make things.
Name a tea brand or tea company.
questions.scope: Real current or historical tea brands, tea companies and tea estates count. A tea variety, drink preparation or generic ingredient is not a company or brand. The inventory includes packaged-tea and ready-to-drink brands; owning a separate brand does not automatically make a generic parent-name guess eligible.

questions.prompt: Name an item that can be used as furnace fuel in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Items actually accepted in the fuel slot count, rather than anything that merely looks flammable. Their fuel value need not be the same. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a color or a named shade.
questions.scope: Recognized English color names and published named shades count, including named pigments, Crayola colors and standard CSS color keywords. Regional spellings and ordinary synonyms share one answer. Patterns are not a single color. Different standard definitions of the same ordinary name do not create extra answers.

questions.prompt: Name a real reservoir or artificial lake.
questions.scope: Named reservoirs and artificial lakes count, including historical and seasonally dry reservoirs. A naturally formed lake does not automatically become a reservoir just because it has a regulated outlet.

questions.prompt: Name an art movement or recognized visual-art style.
questions.scope: Recognized visual-art movements, schools and historical styles count, including architectural and moving-image art movements. An individual artist, work, generic medium or music genre alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a music act known as a duo.
questions.scope: Current and historical musical duos count. Ordinary backing musicians do not change a two-person act into a larger group. Two solo artists who collaborated once are not automatically a named duo.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of songbird.
questions.scope: Recognized kinds, named groups and species count, including documented extinct examples. Common and scientific synonyms share one identity. Age, sex, individual pet names and invented color combinations do not count as kinds.

questions.prompt: Name a medical instrument or piece of medical equipment.
questions.scope: Recognized physical instruments and equipment used for examination, diagnosis, monitoring or treatment count. Medical specialties, diseases, drugs and medical procedures alone do not count. This is an equipment-name question, not treatment advice.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish or preparation in which eggs are a main ingredient.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a Grand Slam singles champion in tennis.
questions.scope: Winners of senior men’s, women’s or wheelchair singles events at the Australian Open, Roland-Garros, Wimbledon or US Open count. Doubles and junior titles alone do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a hairstyle or haircut.
questions.scope: Named, established examples of the whole everyday subject count. Public brand names and actual alternative names share one answer. Generic descriptions or invented combinations do not create new identities.

questions.prompt: Name a real university or college.
questions.scope: Actual named places, institutions, companies or objects in the whole subject count, including documented historical examples. Real public alternative names share one answer. Abbreviations must be actual published names, not generated initials.

questions.prompt: Name a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
questions.scope: All base-game, Echo and DLC fighters count. Pokémon Trainer's three Pokémon, the three Mii fighting styles, and Pyra/Mythra count separately. Alternate costumes share the original fighter's answer; Assist Trophies do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a named character from Rick and Morty.
questions.scope: Named characters belonging to the main official franchise count, including named supporting and one-episode characters. Actors, production credits, fan creations and crossover-only guests do not qualify. Actual public nicknames and personas share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a song with a color in its title.
questions.scope: Ordinary color words in released song titles count; color names used as surnames need context.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can deliver venom.
questions.scope: Venom must be injected or delivered by a bite, sting or spine; simply being poisonous is different.

questions.prompt: Name a programming, scripting, query, markup or stylesheet language.
questions.scope: Real current and historical computer languages for programs, scripts, database queries, markup or style sheets count. Named dialects also count. Plain data-file formats, code editors and ordinary spoken languages do not count. Named XML vocabularies and document-markup formats count; an organization, generic data model, element or software platform alone is not a language.

questions.prompt: Name a player position in a team sport.
questions.scope: Named playing positions from any established team sport count; shared names are one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a real glacier or named glacial ice body.
questions.scope: Real named glaciers, ice caps, icefields and land ice sheets count. Seasonal sea ice, icebergs, mountains without a named ice body and fictional ice are outside this inventory.

questions.prompt: Name an item or trainer device from a Pokémon video game.
questions.scope: Named usable items and trainer devices from released Pokémon video games count, including medicine, Poké Balls, Berries, held/key items, TMs/TRs, evolution items, Pokédexes and trainer communication/navigation devices. Historical versions of the same item name share one answer. Pokémon, moves and Abilities are separate concepts.

questions.prompt: Name a type of fabric or textile material.
questions.scope: Named textile fabrics and textile materials count. Finished garments, towels, sails, loose cut pieces and metal meshes do not count merely because a dictionary groups them under cloth.

questions.prompt: Name a type of chili or bell pepper.
questions.scope: Real named Capsicum pepper kinds/cultivars and documented dried names count. Fresh/dried names of one pepper share identity where they identify the same pepper. Black pepper and arbitrary color-plus-food labels are not Capsicum types.

questions.prompt: Name a mystery TV or streaming show.
Name a song by Coldplay.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Coldplay count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.
